subject: Exception request: Acme model transition pacing and proposed migration sprint
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah McIntyre <sarah@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exception request: Acme model transition pacing and proposed migration sprint

Team —

Quick context: Acme (high-volume embeddings + search, enterprise contract) raised concerns after our deprecation announcement for the v1 model family. Their migration depends on third-party index rebuilds and an internal QA cycle that spans multiple teams. They asked for a longer runway and an explicit plan for pinned access during migration.

What I need from product/ops/legal:
- A short justification and feasibility for a 30–60 day pin (pinned v1 access) for Acme only — what operational risks does this introduce?
- Mitigations we can commit to (rate limits, quota isolation, dedicated routing)
- A concise customer-facing timeline and comms draft we can share with Acme by EOD Friday.

Attachments: [acme-impact-matrix.pdf (summary), proposed-migration-cadence.xlsx (timeline)]

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Internal sync (30 min) to confirm feasibility and ask owners.
2) Send Acme a short update with proposed cadence + ask for their migration ETA.
3) If ops approved, I'll elevate for an exception sign-off from legal and PM leadership.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: Acme model transition pacing and proposed migration sprint

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick heads-up. A few clarifying Qs before we escalate:
- Can you share a rough QPS and token profile for Acme’s calls (embeddings vs. generation)? that helps determine cache/kv footprint.
- Is this request a hard-block (won't migrate) or a preference for extra runway?

From product POV, we have two technical levers:
- temporary pinning of older model behind a routing rule (short-term, low-risk if we throttle), or
- a shim that rewrites calls to a compatible newer family (higher dev overhead, better long-term).

If we go with pinning, we should attach clear SLO/quotas and a sunset window. I can join the sync in 30.

-Rishi
Director, Product Management
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: Acme model transition pacing and proposed migration sprint

Marissa / Rishi —

Operational notes:
- Pinning is feasible but not without cost. We need to reserve capacity (dedicated pool or enforced burst) and add a routing flag plus isolation rules.
- Short-term approach: create a labeled routing rule for customer:acme -> model:v1-pinned for 30 days, with enforced token quota (e.g., 50% of normal) and no autoscaling beyond reserved burst. That keeps other customers protected.
- Longer runway (60 days) increases cost and complexity; requires infra approval and budget sign-off.

I attached the ops runbook snippet that outlines the steps and rollback checklist. If legal okays the exception, we can stand this up in ~48 hours for a limited set of endpoints.

Attachments: [ops-pinning-runbook.md (runbook excerpt)]

-ben
Head of Service Reliability
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah McIntyre <sarah@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exception request: Acme model transition pacing and proposed migration sprint

Sarah —

Thanks for raising this. We understand the rebuild + QA timeline challenges. To keep things moving:
- Would it be possible for you to share a target 2–4 week window when your index team can start acceptance testing? even an approximate week helps us size the pin.
- We'll propose an interim plan: a 30-day pinned access with strict quotas while you run the rebuild. If you need longer, we can evaluate a single 30-day extension after we see usage.
- Can you confirm which endpoints are critical (embeddings/search vs. generation/chat)?

We can jump on a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to walk the cadence. I’ve cc’d procurement so we can align on the billing/credit side if an exception increases unit cost.

Thanks —
Lauren
Customer Success Manager

Thanks everyone — summary and actions: 

Decision points:
- Ops: proceed with a 30-day pin for Acme (routing rule model:v1-pinned) with quotas and no autoscale beyond reserved burst. Ben to open infra ticket and schedule the rollout.
- Product: Rishi to produce a one-page technical note describing impact/risk and a recommended sunset policy (30d + one automatic 30d review).
- Legal: please review the exception terms and confirm if we need an amendment to the contract; target EOD Thurs for sign-off.
- CS/AM: Lauren/Marissa will send Acme a short comms and schedule a migration kickoff call.

Deliverables & owners:
- Ben: infra ticket + runbook execution ETA 48 hours.
- Rishi: one-pager for legal and ops by EOD today.
- Lauren: customer comms draft + proposed call times by EOD today.
- Marissa: escalate for exception approval and capture final sign-off pack (final-exception-request.pdf).

Related links: https://hubspot.example/acme/ACME-2028-R1 (deal), https://drive.example/redwood/acme/migration-plan (working doc)
Attachments: [final-exception-request.pdf (for legal)]

I'll set a short follow-up for Friday to confirm closure. Thanks all for the fast turnaround.

-Marissa
